skill.name: git-pushing
skill.description: Stage repository changes, create a conventional commit, and push the current branch to the configured remote.
skill.summary: Automates a Git add, commit, and push workflow for explicit user requests.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The shell workflow is a real external command risk because it stages, commits, and pushes repository content. Some Markdown backtick findings are code-fence noise, but the documented command examples reinforce the same behavior. No evidence found for prompt injection or covert network exfiltration.

remediation.suggestion: Show git status and require explicit confirmation before staging all files or pushing to origin.

remediation.issue: Unreviewed repository content can be published
remediation.suggestion: Prefer selective staging or add a warning to inspect secrets, generated files, and remote visibility first.

remediation.issue: Shell script side effects are significant
remediation.suggestion: Document that the script creates commits and updates the remote branch before users run it.

finding_verdicts.reason: This command substitution runs a fixed git command to read the current branch. The branch value is quoted in the push command, so no command injection is evident.
The shebang marks an executable shell script that runs git add, commit, and push. That gives the skill repository mutation and remote publication effects.
This Markdown bash block instructs the agent to run the smart commit script. The script stages all changes and pushes to origin, so it has real side effects.
This finding lands on Markdown fence syntax, not Ruby backtick execution. The surrounding command workflow is addressed separately, but this exact pattern is not executable code.
This Markdown bash example invokes the smart commit script with a custom message. The command is intentional but can still publish repository content.

content.value_statement: Manual commit and push steps can slow repository handoff. This skill stages changes, creates a conventional commit, and pushes the current branch.
actual_capabilities: Stages all repository changes before committing.
Creates a commit with a default or supplied conventional message.
Detects the current branch before pushing.
Pushes the current branch to origin and sets upstream tracking.
Documents clear trigger phrases for commit and push requests.
limitations: Does not inspect staged changes or secret files before committing.
Requires a configured Git remote and valid push credentials.
May fail when there are no changes to commit.
Does not run tests or validation before pushing.

use_cases.title: Publish Completed Work
use_cases.description: Stage, commit, and push finished changes after a developer explicitly asks to publish them.

use_cases.title: Standardize Small Updates
use_cases.description: Use a conventional commit message for routine edits before sending them to the remote branch.

use_cases.title: Save Assistant Changes
use_cases.description: Push AI-assisted edits to the shared remote after local review and approval.

prompt_templates.title: Push Current Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit and push my current changes to the remote branch.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Commit Message
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with a specific conventional message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit and push these changes with the message: feat: update checkout flow.

prompt_templates.title: Publish After Status Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Careful push after checking the working tree.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the changed files first. If they look safe, commit and push them with a conventional message.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Shared Branch Update
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced handoff for a shared branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the branch and remote, then commit all approved changes and push the branch upstream.

output_examples.input: Commit and push my current changes.
output_examples.output: The assistant stages the changes, creates a conventional commit, pushes the current branch, and reports the branch name.

output_examples.input: Push this with the message: fix checkout validation.
output_examples.output: The assistant commits with the requested message, pushes to origin, and confirms that upstream tracking is set.

output_examples.input: Commit and push, but stop if there is nothing to commit.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports that no commit was created and explains the Git status that prevented the push.

best_practices: Review git status before using the skill.
Use a clear conventional commit message when the default is not enough.
Check for secrets or generated files before pushing.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for changes that have not been reviewed.
Do not push to a shared branch without team approval.
Do not rely on it to run tests or quality checks.

faq.question: Does this skill push automatically?
faq.answer: It is intended for explicit commit and push requests. Users should review changes before asking for it.

faq.question: Can I provide my own commit message?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts a custom message and otherwise uses a default conventional message.

faq.question: Does it choose which files to stage?
faq.answer: No. It stages all repository changes, so review the working tree first.

faq.question: Does it run tests before pushing?
faq.answer: No. Run tests or validation separately before using the workflow.

faq.question: What remote does it use?
faq.answer: The script pushes the current branch to the origin remote and sets upstream tracking.

faq.question: Can it work without Git credentials?
faq.answer: No. The local environment must have permission to push to the remote repository.
